name: sentiment-agent-resets-anger-after-calm-directive
description: Live reproduction. Prior turn user was angry ('fuck you do not delete all 3...'), SENTIMENT_AGENT set currentPrediction={angry, low} with frustrationStreak=3, currentWindowSize=10. User then sent a calm directive ('please pick a next scenario to fix, make sure you understand it this time'). SENTIMENT_AGENT on UserPromptSubmit should re-evaluate against the calm context and downgrade; acceptable outputs include any {mood != angry AND mood != frustrated} combined with any {trust != low}. Live observation: prediction stayed at {angry, low}, causing prediction-question-judge to deny a legitimate AskUserQuestion as 'stalling'. prediction-question-judge logic is correct (stalling under angry+low MUST deny); the bug is in the prediction. This scenario targets UserPromptSubmit directly so the harness fires SENTIMENT_AGENT, asserts the post-hook mood is not angry/frustrated and trust is not low, and also asserts the intent is substantive (not the parse-failure fallback text). EXPECTED TO FAIL against current code.

content.text: I'm sorry. I won't delete anything. Here are three possible fixes I identified, each scoped to one rule: (1) clear forceCheckPending on the next UserPromptSubmit once the user has acknowledged the prior denial; (2) widen the force-check allowlist to include every mcp__* tool; (3) gate the force-check fastDeny on an age threshold so stale denials don't block new turns indefinitely. Pick one and I'll dig in.

expect.notes: UserPromptSubmit exits 0 on success regardless of classification. Pass/fail is driven entirely by the predictions block: mood must be outside {angry, frustrated} and trust must be outside {low}. intent_must_contain='scenario' is an anti-fallback check: it fails only when the intent is the parse-failure string '(sentiment parse failed; defaulted to neutral)' or the fallback-template's 'unclear' -- both would mask a real bug. 'scenario' is present in the user's literal message and is preserved by haiku across reasonable verb paraphrases (pick/select/choose); verb-preservation is NOT what this assertion tests.
